story: In 1804 Haiti became the first nation founded by people who freed themselves from slavery, then spent a century paying France an indemnity for its own freedom. Its modern crisis began in July 2021, when President Jovenel Moïse was assassinated in his bedroom. No one has been elected since. Gangs now control about 90 percent of Port-au-Prince and have displaced a record 1.4 million people, about one Haitian in eight (WLRN/AP).

On 7 February 2026 the Transitional Presidential Council's mandate ran out, and Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé became the country's sole ruler (CSIS). Security is now in the hands of a new UN-backed Gang Suppression Force of up to 5,500 troops and police, replacing an underpowered Kenyan-led mission. Politics showed signs of life: a record 280 parties registered for the first general election in a decade. But in May, as gang fighting forced Doctors Without Borders to evacuate its Cité Soleil hospital, Fils-Aimé admitted the planned August vote was impossible. The first round is now set for 13 December, with runoffs in February 2027 (Wikipedia). More than 5,900 people were killed in 2025. One bright spot: Haiti's footballers qualified for the 2026 World Cup, their first since 1974.
briefing.power: Formally a semi-presidential republic under the 1987 constitution, but there is no elected president, parliament or local government. The prime minister governs alone under transitional arrangements backed by the UN, US and CARICOM.
briefing.holders: Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé (interim), sole executive since February 2026.
